tasks.short: Review the record, examine and talk with the patient, look up guidelines, make tentative diagnoses and treatment decisions, discuss them with the supervising physician, and explain the plan to the patient.

steps.what: Physician assistant reviews history, findings and results in the record
Physician assistant examines and talks with the patient
Physician assistant looks up the relevant guideline
Physician assistant makes tentative diagnoses and decisions about management and treatment
Physician assistant discusses the plan with the supervising physician
Physician assistant explains the plan to the patient

tasks.design: The record ({OTHER}) shows a problem-oriented summary with active problems, medication, allergies and recent results on one screen, and links the department's guideline for each diagnosis code, so the physician assistant does not search screens and guideline sites. Examining, diagnosing, deciding with the supervising physician and explaining the plan stay with the physician assistant. No software proposes diagnoses.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data were spread over several screens and guidelines searched separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Records can show problem summaries and link guidelines to diagnosis codes.
tasks.still_hard: Problem lists are often out of date.
tasks.human_edge: Sensing that a patient is sicker than the numbers show.

reach.learn: Whether plans arrive with the guideline attached.

evidence.claim: Records can show problem summaries and link guidelines to diagnosis codes.
Decision software is usually a regulated medical device; here no software proposes diagnoses.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient visit to the patient informed; treatment delivery is outside.
Input contract: problem list kept current by the team; fallback is reading screens.
Diagnosing and deciding stay with the physician assistant and physician.
research_questions: Is the guideline consulted more often?

incremental.description: Physician assistant updates the problem list.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: simple visits; high: complex patients with long records.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Open results in the record, compare them with earlier values, interpret deviations from normal, record the interpretation and follow-up, and inform the patient.

steps.what: Physician assistant opens each diagnostic test result in the record
Physician assistant compares results with earlier values
Physician assistant interprets diagnostic test results for deviations from normal
Physician assistant records the interpretation and follow-up
Physician assistant informs the patient of results by phone

tasks.design: New results land in a results inbox in the record ({OTHER}) where fixed rules flag values outside the reference range or with a large change since the last value, and show the trend beside each result, so the physician assistant opens flagged results first and does not page back through earlier values. Follow-up actions are chosen from a short list in the record. Interpreting deviations and informing the patient stay with the physician assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each result was opened and compared with earlier values by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Records flag results by reference range and change, with trend views.
tasks.still_hard: Normal ranges do not fit every patient.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing that a slightly low value matters for this patient.
tasks.altitude: The physician assistant reviews flagged results first.

reach.learn: Whether critical results are acted on sooner.

evidence.claim: Records can flag results by reference range and change since the last value, with trend views.

assumptions: Boundary: from results arrived to the patient informed; treatment changes are outside.
Input contract: reference ranges set by the laboratory; fallback is opening each result.
Every result is still signed off by the physician assistant.
research_questions: Are critical results acted on sooner?

incremental.description: Physician assistant agrees flag rules with the laboratory.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few results with many deviations; high: many normal results.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose the therapy or medication, check interactions and contraindications, write the prescription, obtain the supervising physician's approval, and explain the medication to the patient.

steps.what: Physician assistant chooses therapy or medication
Physician assistant checks interactions and contraindications in the formulary
Physician assistant writes the prescription
Physician assistant obtains physician approval to prescribe therapy or medication
Physician assistant explains the medication to the patient

tasks.design: Medication surveillance in the prescribing module ({OTHER}) checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates against the national drug database rules while the prescription is written, so the physician assistant does not look them up. Order sets per common diagnosis fill the usual dose and duration. Choosing the therapy, obtaining the physician's approval and explaining it to the patient stay with the physician assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Interactions were looked up separately and prescriptions written field by field.
tasks.enabler_now: Rule-based medication surveillance and order sets run in prescribing modules.
tasks.still_hard: Too many alerts get clicked away.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a medicine an elderly patient can manage.

reach.learn: Whether fewer prescriptions need a call back.

evidence.claim: The G-Standaard checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates; KNMP sets the content.
A prescription comes from a named practitioner; software does not prescribe.

assumptions: Boundary: from the treatment plan to the patient instructed; dispensing is outside.
Input contract: drug database loaded in the prescribing module; fallback is looking up.
Approval stays with the supervising physician.

incremental.description: Physician assistant reviews and overrides alerts that do not apply.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: complex patients with many alerts; high: common prescriptions with order sets.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take the history and examine the patient, gather earlier records from other providers, write progress notes and examination findings, and code the diagnosis.

steps.what: Physician assistant obtains health history and performs the physical examination
Physician assistant gathers earlier records and results from other providers by phone and e-mail
Physician assistant records progress notes and results of physical examination

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's consent, and the structured data in the record.
loop.output: A draft progress note with history and examination findings.
loop.check: A validator flags any medication, allergy or value in the draft that does not match the record; the physician assistant edits and approves before the note is saved.
loop.stop: One draft per consult; if the patient declines recording or the draft is rejected, the physician assistant writes the note.
loop.why_not_simpler: History is told in the patient's own words; a form does not capture it.

steps.what: Physician assistant codes the diagnosis in the record

tasks.design: Earlier records and results from other providers are retrieved through the national exchange with the patient's consent, instead of phone and e-mail requests. With consent, a scribe drafts the progress note from the consultation; a validator flags medication, allergies and values that do not match the record, and the physician assistant approves before saving. Diagnosis codes are proposed from the note and confirmed by the physician assistant. Taking the history and examining stay with the physician assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Records were requested by phone and notes typed after each patient.
tasks.enabler_now: Scribes draft notes that clinicians validate and propose codes; national exchanges carry records.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts can add findings that were not examined.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing the detail in the history that changes the diagnosis.
tasks.altitude: The physician assistant validates notes instead of typing.

reach.learn: Whether notes are complete on the day.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber records the consultation and the clinician validates before the note goes into the record.
Juvoly drafts referral letters and suggests ICPC, ICD-10 and SNOMED codes.
At Capio Ramsay Santé, 1,295 clinicians reported time per note falling from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes with Tandem notes; three of seven authors were from the vendor.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient visit to the diagnosis coded; treatment is outside.
Input contract: patient consent for exchange and recording; fallback is phone requests and typing.
The physician assistant approves every note and code.
A DPIA and works council consent come before recording.
research_questions: How long does editing drafted notes take?

incremental.description: Physician assistant asks consent for recording and exchange.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short visits; high: long first consults with outside records.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The physician assistant keeps examining, diagnosing, interpreting results and prescribing with approval; screen searches, look-ups and typed notes shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A physician assistant with more time for patients.
